recipes.name: Panna Cotta with Poached Pears
instructions: In a small bowl, bloom the gelatin by sprinkling it over ¼ cup of the cold milk. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until it wrinkles slightly on the surface. Set aside. - (7 g) envelope unflavored powdered gelatin - ¼ cup whole milk

Meanwhile, in a saucepan, over medium-low heat, combine heavy cream, remaining milk, sugar, salt, and the scraped seeds and pod of the vanilla bean. - 1 ½ cups heavy cream - ¾ cup whole milk - 75 g granulated sugar - of salt - vanilla bean seeds and pod
Heat gently until it just begins to steam. Do not let it boil. - For the Panna Cotta
Remove from the heat and pass through a fine mesh sieve into a heatproof glass bowl. - For the Panna Cotta
Then, whisk the bloomed gelatin in until fully dissolved. - 1 (7 g) envelope unflavored powdered gelatin
Let cool slightly, then pour into the molds. - For the Panna Cotta
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight if you’re the organized type. - For the Panna Cotta
Cut pears in half and remove seeds - pears peeled, halved, cored
In a saucepan over medium heat, combine sherry, brown sugar, and the cinnamon stick. - 2 cups sweet sherry - ½ cup brown sugar - cinnamon stick
Add the pears and poach for 20-25 minutes, flipping halfway, until fork-tender and an amber-color. - 3 pears peeled, halved, cored
Let them cool in the poaching liquid- they will keep in your fridge for up to 2 weeks. - For the Pears

Unmold the set panna cotta by inverting onto a plate. Garnish with a dusting of cinnamon, nutmeg, or any other garnish of your preference. Serve cold alongside poached pears and enjoy! - cinnamon - For the Panna Cotta - For the Pears
